translations.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, toward the west, near the Red Sea, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Aulon, and Zekrisya [?].
It is ten days from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the route through Mount Seir.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses told all the Israelites everything the Lord had commanded him to tell them.
This was after they had killed Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei, beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab.
Moses began to declare this law and said:
The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb and said to us, “You have stayed long enough on this mountain.

Now get up, turn, and enter the hill country of the Amorites and all the settlements of the Arabah, its mountains and its wilderness, the southwest, the coast of the land of Canaan, and the Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
Look, I have given you the land that I swore to give to your ancestors before you—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and to their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
At that time I said to you, ‘I cannot bear you alone.’
For the Lord our God has multiplied us, and look, today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven.
May the Lord, the God of your ancestors, multiply you ten thousand times and bless you as he promised you.
How can I alone bear your trouble, your affairs, and your disputes?
Choose for yourselves wise, discerning, and knowledgeable men from each of your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.
You answered me and said, “This proposal is good,” and you told me, “Do so.”
I took wise, knowledgeable, and discerning men from among you and appointed them over you to be commanders, leaders, rulers of the people, officers, and scribes for your officials.
At that time I told them, “Hear the disputes among your brothers and judge fairly between a man and his brother, and in disputes involving a resident foreigner.

Do not show favoritism in judgment, either to the small or to the great. Judge, and do not show favoritism to anyone, because judgment belongs to God. If a case is too difficult for you, bring it to me, and I will hear it.”
At that time I commanded you concerning everything you were to do.

We set out from Horeb and traveled through all that great and fearsome wilderness you saw, by the route to the hill country of the Amorites, as the Lord our God had commanded us. We reached Kadesh-barnea.
At that time I spoke to you and said, “Go as far as the hill country of the Amorites, which the Lord your God is giving you.
Look and see that the Lord your God has given you the land before you. Now go up and take possession of it, as the Lord, the God of our ancestors, told them. Do not be afraid or dismayed.”
Then all of you came to me and said, “Let us send men ahead of us to inspect the land for us and report back to us about the route by which we should go up and the towns we should enter.”
The proposal pleased me, and I selected twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country, reached the Valley of the Grape Cluster, and inspected it.
They took some of the land’s fruit with them and brought it to us, and we said, “The land the Lord our God is giving us is good.”
But you refused to go up and rebelled against the word of the Lord your God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, “Because the Lord hates us, he brought us out of the land of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites so that they would destroy us.”

Where, then, are we to go up? Your brothers discouraged your hearts and told you, ‘The people are great and numerous, and stronger than we are. Their cities are large, with fortifications reaching up to heaven. We also saw the children of giants there.’
At that time I told you, “Do not be afraid or dismayed because of them.”
The Lord your God will fight alongside you. He goes before you, just as he did everything for you in the land of Egypt.
And in this wilderness you saw how the Lord your God sustained you, as a man sustains his son, all along the road you traveled until you reached this place.
Yet in this matter you did not trust the Lord your God,
who goes before you on the road to choose a place for you and leads you by fire at night to show you the road you should travel, and by a cloud during the day.
The Lord God heard what you said, became angry, and swore, saying:
“These men will not see the blessed land that I swore to give their fathers,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his children the land into which he went up, because his heart is with the Lord.
The Lord was angry with me also because of you, and he told me, ‘You too shall not enter there.’
For Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will enter there. Strengthen him, because he will give Israel that land as an inheritance.
Your children, whom you said would be taken captive, and every little child who today does not know good from evil—they will enter there. I will give it to them, and they will inherit it.”
But you turned back and traveled into the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.

You answered me and said to me, “We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up and fight, just as the Lord our God commanded us.” Each of you took up his weapons of war, and you went up into the mountain.
The Lord said to me, “Tell them: Do not go up or fight, because I am not with you, so that you will not be crushed before your enemies.”
I told you, but you did not listen to me. You disregarded the Lord’s word, acted defiantly, and went up into the mountain.
The Amorites who lived on that mountain came out to meet you, fell upon you, pursued you, and stung you like bees. They struck you down from Seir to Hormah.
You sat and wept before the Lord, but he did not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
You stayed in Kadesh for many days, as long as you had stayed there before.
Then we turned back and traveled into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea, as the Lord had told me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
The Lord said to me:
“You have gone around this mountain long enough. Now turn toward the north.
Command the people and tell them, ‘Look, you are passing through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, and they will be very afraid of you.’
Take care not to fight with them, because I will not give you any of their land as an inheritance, not even a footstep’s worth, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his portion.
Buy food from them with your money and eat it. Also obtain measured quantities of water from them with your money and drink it.

For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. Remember how you crossed this great and terrifying wilderness. Look, for forty years the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing that you asked for.”

We passed by your brothers, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, along the road of the Arabah from Elom and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and traveled along the road through the wilderness of Moab.

The Lord said to me, “Do not be hostile to the Moabites or fight with them, because I will not give you any of their land as an inheritance, because I have given Seir to the descendants of Lot as their inheritance.”
The Emim formerly lived in it, a very great people, strong like those in [?].
They too are Rephaim, like those in Akim [?], and the Moabites call them Zamin.

The Horites formerly lived in Seir, but the descendants of Esau destroyed them and crushed them before them, and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land of their inheritance that the Lord gave them.
“Now get up, move on, and go into the valley of Zered.” And we crossed the valley of Zered.

The time from when we traveled from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the valley of Zered was thirty-eight years, until all the fighting men of that generation had died and disappeared from the camp, as the Lord God had sworn to them.
For the hand of the Lord was against them, to destroy them from the camp until they had fallen.
And when all those fighting men had fallen and died from among the people,
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Look, you are passing into the territory of Moab, which is in Seir.

When you come near the Ammonites, do not antagonize them or engage in battle with them, for I will not give you any of the Ammonites’ land as a possession. I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their allotted portion.
It is counted as a land of the Rephaim, because the Rephaim lived in it formerly, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
They were a great and numerous people, strong and mighty like the Anakim. The Lord destroyed them before the Ammonites, who dispossessed them and settled in their place.
So they did for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir: the Lord destroyed the Horites before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place to this day.
As for the Hivites who lived in Hazeroth as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians destroyed them and settled in their place.

Now rise, move on, and cross the valley of the Arnon. Look, I have handed over to you Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, and his land. Take possession of it and inherit it; engage them and fight them.
On this day I will begin to make all the nations under heaven fear you and tremble before you. They will be terrified when they hear your name, and fear will seize them before you.”
You sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying:
“Let me pass through your land. I will travel along the road and will not turn aside to the right or to the left,
Sell me food for my gold, so that I may eat, and sell me water for my gold, so that I may drink. I will only pass through on foot.
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Aroer allowed me to do, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord our God has given us.”
But Sihon king of Heshbon refused to let us pass through his territory, because the Lord our God hardened his spirit and made his heart evil, so that he would be handed over to us on that day.
The Lord said to me, “Look, I have begun to hand over to you Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, and his land before you. Begin to take possession of his land as your inheritance.”
Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, to fight us at Jahaz.
The Lord our God handed him over to us, and we killed him, all his sons, and all his people.
We captured all his towns at that time and destroyed all his towns, together with their women and children. We left none of them alive.
Except for their livestock, which we took as spoil for ourselves; and we plundered the cities we captured.
From Aroer, beyond the Arnon River, and the town in the valley, as far as Mount Gilead, there was no town that escaped us, for the Lord our God handed over all the towns to us.
But we did not enter the land of the Ammonites, or any of the territory along the Jabbok River, or the towns in [?], as the Lord our God had commanded us.
We turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, at Edrei, to fight us.

The Lord said to me, “Do not fear him, for I will hand him over to you, together with all his people and all his land. You will do to him as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
And the Lord our God delivered Og king of Bashan and all his people into our hands, and we killed them until we left him no offspring.
We captured all his cities in those days. There was no city that we did not take from them: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fortified, with high walls, gates, and bars, besides the very many towns of the Perizzites.
We utterly destroyed them, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon. We destroyed all the cities together, including their women and children, until we left no survivor.
And all their livestock and the plunder that we took from their cities.
In those days we took their land from the hands of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon River—as they call it—to Hermon.
The Phoenicians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.
All the cities of the kingdom of [?] Mishor, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, the cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan;
which the Rephaim left behind. Look, his bed was an iron bed, and it is in the territory of the descendants of Ammon. It is nine cubits long and four cubits wide, measured by a man's cubit.
We plundered that land in those days. From Aroer, which is beside the Arnon River, together with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities, I gave it to Reuben and Gad.
The rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og's kingdom, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, including the whole region of Argob. All this Bashan is counted as the land of the Rephaim.

Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Girgashites and the Maacathites. He named the settlements of Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair, as they are called to this day.
And I gave Gilead to Machir.
To Reuben and Gad I gave the land from Gilead to the Arnon River, with the middle of the river as the boundary, and as far as the Jabbok River, the boundary of the descendants of Ammon.
And the Arabah and the Jordan, with their boundary from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, from Ashdoth-pisgah on the east.

In those days I commanded you and said to you, 'The Lord your God has given you this land as your allotted possession. All your warriors are to go with your weapons of war ahead of your brothers, the descendants of Israel.'
But your wives and your children—and I know that you have many livestock—shall remain in your cities, which I gave you,

until the Lord our God gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too possess the land that the Lord our God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then all of you shall return to your inheritance, which I gave you.
At that time I also commanded Joshua and told him, ‘Your eyes have seen everything the Lord did to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to every kingdom into which you go.’
Do not be afraid of them, for the Lord will fight them for you.
In those days I pleaded with the Lord and said to him:

O Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your strength and your power, the strength of your hand and the greatness of your arm. What god is there in heaven or on earth who does what you have done?
Let me cross over and see that blessed land beyond the Jordan, that blessed mountain, and the Anti-Lebanon.
But the Lord refused to listen to me and did not hear me. The Lord said to me, 'You have had enough. Do not speak of this matter again.'
Go up to the top of the rocky height and look with your eyes toward the west, north, south, and east. Look with your own eyes, because you will not cross this Jordan.
Give Joshua his instructions and strengthen him, for he will cross over ahead of this people of mine, and he will give them possession of the land that you have seen.
And we stayed in the ravine near Beth-peor.

And now, Israel, listen to his statutes and judgments, which I am teaching you today, so that you may follow them, live, increase in number, and enter and possess the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
Do not add to the word that I command you today, and do not take anything away from it, so that you may keep all the commandments of the Lord your God.
Your own eyes have seen everything that the Lord our God did at Baal-peor, for the Lord your God destroyed from among you every man who followed Baal-peor.
But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today.
Look, see the statutes and judgments I have shown you, as the Lord commanded me. Act accordingly in the land you are entering to possess.
Keep them and carry them out, for this is your wisdom and understanding before all the nations who will hear all these statutes and say, “Look, this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”
And what great nation has a god who draws near to it as the Lord our God does whenever we call upon him?
And what great nation has statutes and judgments as righteous as this entire law that I am setting before you today?

Be mindful of yourself and guard your soul carefully, so that you do not forget all these things that your eyes have seen, and they do not depart from your heart throughout your life. Teach them to your children and your children’s children.

And tell them about the day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, on the day you assembled. For the Lord said to me, “Gather the people to me, and let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the earth, and may teach their children.”
You came and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain burned with fire reaching to heaven, amid darkness, storm, and mist.
The Lord spoke to me from the midst of the fire, and you heard his voice as he spoke, but you saw no form—only his voice.
He made known to you his covenant, which he commanded you to carry out: the ten words. He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the Lord also commanded me to teach you statutes and judgments to carry out in the land you are entering to possess.
Guard yourselves very carefully, for you saw no form on the day when the Lord spoke to you at Horeb, on the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
Do not go astray or make yourselves a carved image in the likeness of any figure, in the likeness of a male or a female,
in the likeness of any animal on the earth, or in the likeness of any winged bird that flies beneath heaven;
or in the likeness of any living creature that moves on the earth, or in the likeness of any fish in the water beneath the earth.

And if you look up to heaven and see the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the ornaments of heaven, beware lest you go astray and bow down to them and worship them, which the Lord your God made for all the nations under heaven.
But the Lord took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, so that you would be his own people, as you are to this day.
The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and swore that I would not cross this Jordan or enter the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I will die in this land and will not cross the Jordan, but you will cross and possess that blessed land.

So take care that you do not forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which he made with you, and sin by making yourselves a carved image in the likeness of anything against which the Lord your God warned you.
For the Lord your God is a consuming fire and a jealous God.

When you have had sons and daughters and grandchildren, and have grown old in the land, and you sin and make yourselves a likeness of anything, and do evil before the Lord your God to provoke him to anger,

look, I call heaven and earth to witness against you that you will perish and be wiped out from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live there for many days, but will be utterly destroyed.
The Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations into which the Lord brings you.
There you will worship foreign gods, the work of human hands, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
Then you will seek the Lord your God there, and you will find him when you seek him with all your heart and all your soul in your suffering.
All these things will happen to you in the last days, and you will return to the Lord your God, and he will hear you.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God. He will not abandon you or destroy you, and he will not forget the covenant with your ancestors that the Lord swore to them.

Ask about the earlier days, which were before your time, from the day when God created humankind on the earth, from one end of heaven to the other: Has anything like this ever happened? Has there ever been anything like it?
Has any people heard the voice of the Lord, the living God, speaking from the midst of the fire, as you heard it, and remained alive?

Has the Lord ever undertaken to go and take for himself a people from among another people, through trials, signs, wonders, warfare, a mighty hand, an uplifted arm, and great terrors, like everything the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you, while you watched?
So that you may know that the Lord is God, and there is no other besides him.
His voice was heard from heaven to teach you, and on earth he showed his great fire, and you heard his voice from the midst of the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors and chose their descendants after them—you—from among all the nations, he himself brought you out of Egypt by his great power,
to destroy great and powerful nations before you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as you have it today.
Know today that the Lord God is the Lord in heaven above and on earth below, and there is no other besides him.

Keep his statutes and his commandments, which I command you today, so that all may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that your days may be long in the land that the Lord your God gives you for all time.
At that time Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
so that a person who had killed another unintentionally, without previously being his enemy, could flee there. He could flee to one of these cities and remain alive.
Bezer in the wilderness, in the open country, for Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead for Gad; and Golan in Bashan for Manasseh.
This is the law that Moses commanded the Israelites in their presence.
These are all the commandments, statutes, and judgments that Moses spoke to the Israelites in the wilderness when they came out of the land of Egypt,
beyond the Jordan, in the valley near Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites killed when they came out of the land of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.
From Aroer, which is across the River Arnon, as far as Mount Sion, which is Hermon,
all the Arabah beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, below Asedon, which has a wall.
Moses called all Israel and said to them, ‘Listen, Israel, to all the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing today, on this day. Learn to carry them out and keep them.’
The Lord your God established his covenant with you at Horeb.
He did not establish this covenant with your ancestors, but with you, for you are here today, all of you alive.
The Lord spoke to you face to face on the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
I stood between the Lord and you on that day to tell you the word of the Lord, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain.
He said, “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods besides me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved god or any likeness of anything in heaven above, or anything on the earth below, or anything in the water beneath the earth.
Do not bow down to them or worship them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, who punishes children for their parents’ sin to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
And I show mercy to ten thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
Do not swear falsely by the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not acquit anyone who swears falsely by his name.
Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
For six days you shall work and do all your work.

The seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any of your work, neither you nor your son nor your daughter nor your male servant nor your female servant nor your ox nor your donkey nor any of your livestock nor the foreigner within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there with a strong hand and a raised arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that things may go well for you and your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God gave you.
Do not go to another man's wife. Do not kill anyone. Do not steal. Do not be a false witness against your neighbor. Do not falsify testimony.

Do not desire your neighbor’s wife, and do not desire your neighbor’s house, his field, his male slave, his female slave, his ox, his donkey, any of his livestock, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

These are the words the Lord spoke to your entire assembly on the mountain, from the midst of fire, darkness, storm, and thick cloud, with a loud voice. He added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets, and the Lord gave them to me.
When you heard that voice from the midst of the fire, while the mountain was burning with fire, all of you—the representatives of your tribes and your elders—came to me.

You said to me, “Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory, and we have heard his voice from the midst of the fire. Today, on this day, we have learned that God speaks with human beings and they remain alive.
And now, let us not die, and let this great fire not destroy us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God again, then we will die.
For what mortal has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of fire, as we have, and remained alive?
Go yourself and hear everything that the LORD our God says. Then tell us everything that the LORD our God tells you, and we will listen and do it.”
The LORD heard the words you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, “I have heard the words of this people, everything they said to you. Everything they have said is right.
If only they could remain like this, fearing me and keeping my commandments all their days, so that things would go well for them and their children forever!
Go and tell them, ‘Go into your houses.’”
But you, stand beside me. I will tell you all my commandments, statutes, and laws, which you are to teach them so that they may follow them in the land I am giving them as their inheritance.
Be careful to do as the LORD your God commanded me, and do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Along the whole path that the Lord your God commanded you to follow, so that things may go well for you, that you may have rest, and that your days may be long in the land you will inherit.
This is the commandment, and all the statutes and laws that the LORD our God commanded me to teach you to carry out in the land you are entering to possess.

This is so that you may fear the LORD your God and keep all his statutes and all his commandments that I command you today—you, your son, and your son’s children—all the days of your life, so that your days may be long.

Listen, Israel, and be careful to carry them out, so that things may go well for you, your days may be long, and you may multiply greatly, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, said that he would give you a land flowing with milk and honey. This is the commandment and all the statutes that Moses commanded the Israelites in the wilderness after they came out of the land of Egypt.
Listen, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.
Love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
Let all these words that I tell you today remain in your heart and in your soul.
Teach them to your son and speak of them when you sit in the house, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Make them a sign on your hands, and let them remain immovable before your eyes.
Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
And when the Lord your God brings you into the land that the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you—great and fine cities that he did not build;

and houses filled with every good thing that you did not store up, and dug cisterns that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant—and after you have eaten and are satisfied;
then take care not to forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Fear the Lord your God, worship him alone, follow him, and swear by his name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the nations around you.
For the Lord your God is a jealous God. Take care that the Lord your God does not turn against you in his anger and uproot you from the face of the earth.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test as you tested him on the day of testing.
Be watchful and keep the commandment of the Lord your God, and obey all his ordinances that he commanded you;
Do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God, so that things may go well for you and you may enter and inherit the blessed land that the Lord swore to your fathers.
so that he may drive out all your enemies before you, as the Lord said.
And when your son asks you tomorrow, saying to you, “What are all these commandments, ordinances, and laws that the Lord our God commanded us?”
you shall tell your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in the land of Egypt, and [the Lord] brought us out of there with a mighty hand and a raised arm.
The Lord sent great and terrible signs and wonders against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against his household, before our eyes.
He brought us out of there to bring us into this land and give it to us, as he swore to give it to our fathers.
And the Lord commanded us to carry out all these ordinances and to fear the Lord our God, so that things would go well for us all our days and so that we would live, as we do today;
and so that we would find mercy if we were careful to carry out all these commandments before the Lord our God, as the Lord commanded us.”

And when the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are going to possess, and removes great and numerous nations from before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven great nations stronger than us;
and the Lord your God delivers them into your hands and you kill them, you must destroy them completely. Do not make a covenant with them, and do not show them mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughter to his son, and do not take his daughter for your son.
For he will turn your son away from me, and your son will worship other gods. The Lord's anger will burn against you, and he will quickly destroy you.
Instead, do this to them: tear down their altars, smash their images, [cut down their sacred groves,] and burn their carved gods with fire.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God. The Lord your God singled you out and chose you to be his people from among all the nations on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the nations that the Lord chose you in preference to them, for you are fewer than all the nations.

Rather, because the Lord loved you and because he keeps the oath he swore to your fathers, the Lord your God brought you out with a mighty hand and a raised arm, and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Know that the Lord your God is the Lord, and that he is a faithful God who keeps his covenant and his mercy toward those who love him and keep his commandments, for ten thousand generations;
He will repay those who hate him to their faces and destroy them. He will not delay the destruction of those who hate him, but will confront them directly.
Keep all his commandments, statutes, and laws that I command you today, and carry them out.
and if you listen to these ordinances of his, keep them, and carry them out, the Lord will keep for you his covenant and his mercy that he swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and make you numerous. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land, your wheat, your wine, your oil, the pastures of your cattle, and the grazing grounds of your sheep, in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give you.
You will be blessed above all nations. None of your women will be barren or without children, nor will any of your livestock be barren.

The Lord will remove every disease from you. He will not bring upon you any of the terrible illnesses that you saw come upon Egypt. He will turn all those illnesses you saw away from you and bring them upon your enemies and all who hate you.
You will consume the spoils of the nations that the Lord your God gives you. Your eye must not pity them, and you must not worship their gods, because this would be evil for you.
If you say in your heart, “These people are numerous. How can I destroy them?”
Do not fear them. Be sure to remember everything the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

the great trials that your eyes saw, and those signs and great wonders, with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, by which the Lord your God brought you out of there. The Lord your God will do the same to all the nations whose presence you fear.
The Lord your God will send a plague upon them ahead of you, until he destroys those who remain and those who hide from you.
Do not be terrified of them, because the Lord your God is with you, and he is a great and mighty God.

The Lord your God will destroy these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to destroy them quickly, so that the land does not become deserted and the wild animals multiply against you.
The Lord your God will deliver them into your hands and crush them with great destruction until he has destroyed them.
He will deliver their kings into your hands and wipe out their names from that place. No one will be able to stand against you until the Lord has destroyed them.

Burn all the carved images of their gods with fire. Do not desire either the gold or the silver from them, and do not take it for yourself, so that you do not fall into sin through them, because they are unclean in the sight of the Lord your God.
Do not bring an unclean thing into your house and become accursed like it. Regard it as utterly unclean and utterly detest it, for it is accursed.
Be careful to carry out every commandment that I give you today, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and possess the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors.
Remember the whole journey on which the Lord your God led you through the wilderness, to afflict you and test you, and to know your heart—whether you would keep his commandment or not.

He afflicted you and made you hungry, and then fed you with manna, which your ancestors did not know, to show you that people do not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not become dirty during these forty years.
Know in your heart that, just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you.
Keep all the commandments of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the Lord your God will bring you into a blessed and plentiful land, with streams of water and deep springs like the sea, flowing through the wilderness and the mountains.
A land of wheat and barley, vineyards, figs and pomegranates; a land of olive trees, oil and honey;
a land where you will not eat your bread in scarcity and where you will lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron and from whose mountains they extract copper.
Eat and be satisfied, and bless the Lord your God in the blessed land that he has given you.
Watch yourself and do not forget the Lord your God. Keep his commandment, his law and all his judgments that I command you today.
Otherwise, when you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built fine houses and lived in them,
and your sheep and cattle have multiplied, and your gold and silver have increased, and all your possessions have increased,
Otherwise your heart may become proud, and you may forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

He led you through that great and terrifying wilderness, with its biting wild animals and scorpions, its thirst and lack of drinking water. He brought a spring of fresh water out of the hard rock for you.
He fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and test you, and to do good to you in your later days.
Do not say in your heart, “By my strength and the power of my hands I have gained this great wealth for myself.”
Remember the Lord your God, because he is the one who gives you strength, so that he may uphold his covenant, which the Lord swore to your ancestors, as it is today.
If you do indeed forget the Lord your God and follow other gods, serve them, and bow down to them, I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will surely perish.
Like all the nations that the Lord destroyed before you, you too will be destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Listen, Israel! Today you are about to cross the Jordan, to go and dispossess great nations stronger than you, and take great cities whose towering walls reach to heaven.
A great and tall people [the descendants of Anak], to whom you say [?].
Know today that the Lord your God goes before you. He is a consuming fire. He will overthrow them and uproot them before you; he will make them perish and destroy them quickly, as the Lord told you.

When the Lord has destroyed those nations before you, do not say in your heart, “Because of my righteousness the Lord brought me in to take possession of this blessed land.” Rather, because of those nations’ sins, the Lord destroyed them before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the purity of your heart that you are entering to take possession of their land. Rather, because of those nations’ sins, the Lord will destroy those nations before you, and so uphold his covenant, which the Lord swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know today that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God gives you that blessed land to possess, for you are a stubborn people.

Remember, and do not forget, how much you angered the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day he brought you out of the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the Lord.
At Horeb too, you angered the Lord, and the Lord became angry enough with you to destroy you.

When they went up the mountain so that I could receive the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no food and drank no water.
The Lord gave me two stone tablets inscribed with the finger of the Lord. On them were written all the words the Lord spoke to us on the mountain on the day you assembled.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

The Lord said to me, “Get up and go quickly from here, because your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have sinned. They have quickly turned away from the path you commanded them to follow. They have made themselves a cast-metal image.”
The Lord said to me, “I tell you once and again: I have seen this people, and they are a stubborn people.
Leave me alone, so that I may destroy them and erase their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a great and strong nation, far more numerous than this one.”
I turned and came down from the mountain. The mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets were in my two hands.
When I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God, had made yourselves a cast-metal image, and had abandoned the path that the Lord commanded you to follow;
I took those two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and shattered them before you.

Again I pleaded before the Lord, as before, for forty days and forty nights. I ate no food and drank no water because of all your sins, which you committed, and the evil you did before the Lord your God to provoke him to anger.
I feared the anger with which the Lord was angry against you, intending to destroy you. But the Lord listened to me at that time.
The Lord was also very angry with Aaron, intending to destroy him. I also prayed for Aaron at that time.

As for your sinful deed, the calf you had made, I took it, broke it to pieces, and ground it thoroughly until I had crushed it very finely and it became like dust. I threw its ground remains into the stream that flows down from the mountain.
At the burning, at the time of testing, and at the memorial of craving, you provoked the Lord your God to anger.

And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said to you, "Go up and take possession of the land I am giving you," you rebelled against the word of the Lord your God. You did not trust him or listen to his voice.
You have been rebellious against the Lord from the day he became known to you.
I pleaded before the Lord for forty days and forty nights, as I had pleaded before, because the Lord had said he would destroy you.

I prayed to the Lord and said, "Lord, King of the gods, do not destroy your people, your own portion, whom you redeemed by your great power and brought out of Egypt by your great power, your strong hand, and your uplifted arm."
Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself. Do not look at this people's wickedness, their wrongdoing, or their sin,

so that the inhabitants of the land from which you brought us out will not say, 'The Lord was unable to bring them into the land he had promised them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.'
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt by your great power and your strong, uplifted arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, 'Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, come up to me on the mountain, and make a wooden ark.'
I will write on these tablets all the words that were on the earlier tablets you broke. Put them in the ark.
I made an ark of wood that does not decay and carved two stone tablets like the first ones. [?] went up the mountain, with those two tablets in my hands.
He wrote on those tablets, just as in the first writing, the ten commandments that the Lord had spoken to us on Mount Sinai from the midst of the fire.
I put those tablets, which I had made, into the ark, and they remained there, as the Lord had commanded me.
The Israelites traveled from Beeroth of the sons of Jaakan [?] Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar was appointed priest there in his place.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the Lord's law, to stand before the Lord and serve, and to pray in his name, as they do to this day.
For this reason the Levites have no share or inheritance with their brothers, because the Lord is their share, as he told them.
I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. The Lord listened to me during those days too, and the Lord spared you and did not destroy you.
The Lord said to me, 'Go and speak before this people, so that they may enter and take possession of the land that I swore to their ancestors I would give them.'
And now, Israel, what does the Lord require of you except to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul,
and to keep the commandments of the Lord your God and all his ordinances that I command you today, so that it may go well with you?
Look, heaven, the heaven of heavens, the earth, and everything in it belong to the Lord your God.
Yet the Lord preferred your ancestors and loved them, and he chose their descendants after them—you—out of all the nations, as it is to this day.
Circumcise the evil from your hearts, then, and no longer stiffen your necks.
For the Lord your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome Lord, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
He provides justice for the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow. He loves the foreign resident and gives him food and clothing.
Love the foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreign residents in the land of Egypt.
Fear the Lord your God, worship him alone, follow him, and swear by his name.
For he is your source of pride, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and glorious things that your eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down into Egypt as seventy people, but now the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.
Love the Lord your God and keep his law, statutes, commandments, and judgments throughout all the days of your life.
Know today that it was not your children who saw and knew the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness, his mighty hand, and his uplifted arm;
and his signs and all his wonders that he performed in the midst of Egypt, against Pharaoh king of Egypt and throughout his land;
and everything he did to Egypt’s army, its chariots, and its horses—how the waters of the Red Sea covered them as they pursued you from behind, and the Lord your God destroyed them, down to this day;
and everything he did for you in the wilderness until you reached this place;

and everything he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and all their possessions that were with them, from the midst of all Israel.
For your own eyes have seen all the great deeds that the Lord has done.
Keep every commandment of his that I command you today, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and take possession of the land for which you are crossing the Jordan, to possess it there;
So that your days may be long in the land that the Lord swore to give to your fathers and their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came, where, when they sow seed, they water it with their feet like a vegetable garden.
But the land you are entering to possess is a land of mountains and plains, watered by the rain from heaven;
a land that the Lord your God continually watches over. The eyes of the Lord your God are upon it from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
If you faithfully obey every commandment that I command you today, loving the Lord your God and serving him with all your heart and all your soul;
he will give rain upon your land in its proper seasons, both the early and the late rain, and will enable you to gather your grain, your wine, and your oil;
he will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
But take care that you do not let your hearts grow proud, become unfaithful, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them.
And the Lord will become angry with you and shut the sky, so that no rain comes and the earth does not yield its fruit, and you will quickly perish from the blessed land that the Lord has given you.
Keep this word in your hearts and in your souls. Place it as a sign on your hands, and let it remain fixed before your eyes.
Teach it to your children so that they speak about it when they sit in the house and when they walk along the road, and when you lie down and when you rise.
Write it on the doorframes of your houses;
so that your days and the days of your children may be many in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give them, as long as the heavens remain above the earth.
And if you faithfully obey every commandment that I give you today, carrying them out, loving the Lord your God, walking in all his ways, and following him;
The Lord will drive these nations out before you, and you will dispossess great nations that are stronger than you.
Every place where your feet tread will be yours. From the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, and from the great river, the Euphrates, to the sea toward the west, will be your territory.
No one will be able to stand against you. The Lord will put fear and dread of you over the whole land on which you set foot, as the Lord told you.
Look, today I set before you a blessing and a curse:
a blessing if you obey all the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today;
and a curse if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today, but abandon the path that I command you today and go and worship other gods whom you do not know.
When the Lord your God brings you into the land for which you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of it, you shall place the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These are beyond the Jordan, behind the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, near the tall trees.
Look, you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of the land that the Lord your God gives you as your allotted possession for all time, and you shall live in it.
Be careful to carry out all his commandments and judgments and everything that I set before you today.

These are the commandments and judgments that you must carefully carry out in the land that the Lord your God gives you as your allotted possession, throughout all the days that you live on the earth.
You must completely destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing worshiped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under leafy trees.
Tear down their altars, smash their images, cut down their trees, burn the carved images of their gods with fire, and erase their names from that place.
And you must not do this to the Lord your God.
Except in the place that the Lord has chosen, in one of your cities, for his name to be named there;
and you shall bring your sacrifices, your offerings, your firstfruits, your vowed gifts, your voluntary gifts, what you give with your right hand, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep.
Eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in everything to which you have put your hands, you and your households, because the Lord your God has blessed you.
Do not do everything that we do here today, each person doing what pleases him.
For you have not yet reached your resting place and the inheritance that the Lord your God gives you.
Cross the Jordan and live in the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you will live securely.

At the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be named there, you shall bring everything that I command you today: your sacrifices, your offerings, your tithes, the firstfruits of your hands, your gifts, the choicest of all your offerings, and everything that you have vowed to your God.
Rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites within your gates, because they have no share or inheritance with you.
Be careful not to offer your sacrifices in every place you see.
Instead, offer your sacrifices at the place that the Lord your God chooses within one of your tribes. There you shall do everything that I command you today.

You may slaughter whatever you desire there and eat meat in all your cities, according to the blessing that the Lord has given you. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it together, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
But do not eat the blood. Pour it onto the ground like water.

You must not eat in any of your towns the tithe of your wine, grain, or oil, the firstborn of your cattle or sheep, any of the offerings you have vowed, your voluntary offerings, or the firstfruits of your hands.

Eat them before the Lord your God in the place the Lord your God has chosen—you, your sons, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, and the foreign resident in your town. Rejoice before the Lord your God in everything you put your hand to.
Be careful not to abandon the Levite as long as you live on the earth.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he told you, and you say, “I will eat meat,” because you desire to eat meat, you may eat meat as much as you desire.

If the place the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be named there is far away, you may slaughter animals from your cattle and sheep that the Lord your God has given you, as I commanded you, and eat in your town as much as you desire.
Eat it as you eat a gazelle or a deer. Both the unclean and the clean among you may eat it alike.
Be very careful not to eat the blood, because the blood is its life, and the life must not be eaten with the meat.
Do not eat it; pour it onto the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
But take what you have set apart as holy and what you have vowed, and go to the place the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be named there.
Prepare your offerings and place their meat on the altar. Pour the blood of your sacrifice beside the altar of the Lord your God, and eat some of its meat.
Keep and obey every word that I command you today, so that it may go well with you and your children forever, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
And when the Lord your God destroys before you the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you dispossess them and live in their land;
Be careful not to desire to follow them after they have been destroyed before you. Do not desire their gods, and do not say, “I too will do what these nations do for their gods.”
Do not do the same for the Lord your God, because the Lord hates the unclean things the nations do for their gods. They even burn their sons and daughters in fire for their gods.
Be careful to carry out every word that I command you today. Do not add to it or take away from it.
If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and performs a sign or a wonder—
And his sign or wonder that he told you about comes to pass, while he says, “Come, let us go and worship gods that you do not know”;
Do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, because the Lord your God is testing you to see whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
Follow the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, listen to his voice, and take refuge in him.

That prophet or dreamer of dreams must die, because he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from slavery, and because he sought to forsake the path in which the Lord your God commanded you to walk. You must uproot and destroy the evil from among you.

If your brother, whether from your father or your mother, or your son, your daughter, the wife who lies in your embrace, or your friend whom you love as yourself urges you secretly, saying, “Come, let us go and worship other gods,” which neither you nor your ancestors have known—
Some of the gods of the nations around you, whether near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other—
Do not join him or listen to him. Do not look on him with pity or show him mercy.
Make it known and report him. Your hands must be the first to kill him, and afterward the hands of all the people must stone him.
They must kill him, because he wanted to lead you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
All Israel will hear and be afraid, and they will no longer do evil among you.
If you hear people saying, in one of your cities that the Lord your God has given you to live in:
“Sinful men have gone out from among us and led astray all those who live in their cities, saying to them, ‘Come, let us go and worship other gods whom you do not know,’”
you must investigate and inquire thoroughly. If it proves true and the report is confirmed that something unclean has happened among you,
you must kill all those who live in that city with the sword, and place it and everything in it under the curse of destruction.

Gather all its goods into its streets and burn the city with fire, together with all its goods. Treat the whole city in this way before the Lord your God. No one shall ever live in it, and it shall not be rebuilt.

Do not take into your hand anything in it that is under the curse, so that the Lord may turn away from his anger, grant you mercy, have compassion on you, and multiply you, as the Lord swore to your ancestors,
(so that) if you faithfully obey the voice of the Lord your God, keep all his commandments—all that I command you today—and do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
You are children of the Lord your God. Do not shave your heads for someone who has died.
For you are a holy people belonging to the Lord your God. The Lord your God has chosen you from all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his own people.
Do not eat anything unclean.
These are the animals you may eat: an ox, a sheep from the flock, and a kid from the goats;
the deer, the gazelle, the wild ox, [?], the ibex, the oryx, and the giraffe.
You may eat any animal whose hoof is split and divided into two hoof-halves, and which chews the cud.

But these you must not eat from among those that chew the cud or have split hooves divided into two: the camel, the hare, and the rock hyrax. They chew the cud, but their hooves are not split; they are unclean for you.
The wolf also is unclean for you, because its hoof is split and divided, but it does not chew the cud. Do not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses.
And this is what you may eat from the water: eat anything that has fins and scales.
But do not eat anything that has no fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
Eat every clean bird.
And these are the birds you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the sea eagle;
And the griffon vulture, [?], and others of its kind;
and the raven and others of its kind;
and the ostrich, the owl, and the gull;
and the heron, the swan, and the ibis;
and the cormorant, the stork and others of its kind, the hoopoe, and the owl;
and the pelican, the plover and others of its kind, the purple swamphen, and the bat.
All these birds are unclean for you, and you must not eat any of them.
Eat any of the clean birds.

Do not eat anything that has died on its own. Give it to the foreign resident in your town so that he may eat it, or give it to a foreigner, because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. Do not boil a calf in its mother's milk.
You must set aside a tenth of all the grain you sow that comes from your fields each year.

Eat it each year before the Lord your God, in the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be invoked there. Bring the tenth of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.

But if the journey is too long for you and you cannot carry it, because the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be invoked there is far away from you, because the Lord your God blesses you,
then turn it into silver, take the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the Lord your God has chosen.
Pay for whatever you desire—cattle, sheep, wine, mead, or anything else you desire. Eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your household,
and the Levite who is in your town, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
In the third year, bring in the whole tenth of your grain, and store it in your town in that year.

Then the Levite will come to you, because he has no share or inheritance with you, along with the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow who are in your town, so that they may eat and so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work you do.
In the seventh year, you must cancel debts.

This is the command concerning the cancellation: all that your neighbor owes you is to be canceled. Do not demand repayment from your brother, because a cancellation has been proclaimed for the Lord your God.
You may demand from a foreigner all that he owes you, but you must cancel what your brother owes you.
For there will be no poor person among you, because the Lord your God will surely bless you in the land that the Lord your God gives you as your allotted inheritance,
if you diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God and keep and carry out this whole command that I give you today.
For the Lord your God has blessed you as he told you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
And if there is someone impoverished among your brothers in one of your towns that the Lord your God has given you, do not turn your heart away or close your hand against giving to your brother.
Instead, open your hand wide and give your brother what he asks of you, from what he asks of you.

Guard yourself so that there is no sinful thought in your heart, saying, “The year of cancellation, the seventh year, is near,” and he gives him nothing, and your brother looks at you with hostility and cries out against you to the Lord, and you become guilty of sin.

Instead, you must give to him freely and lend to him freely, as much as he asks of you. Do not be grieved in your heart when you give to him, because for this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you put your hand to.

For poor people will never be absent from the land. Therefore I command you today to do this, and I tell you to open your hand wide to your poor brother and to your neighbor in your land who asks you for help.
If your fellow Hebrew, whether a man or a woman, is sold to you, that person must serve you for six years, and in the sixth year you must set that person free and send them away from you.
Do not send that person away empty-handed.
Provide that person generously with supplies from your sheep, your grain, and your winepress. Give according to how much the Lord your God has blessed you.
And remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there. For this reason I command you to do this.
But if he tells you that he will not leave you, because he loves you and your household, and because living with you is better for him,
then take an awl and pierce his ear at the door, at the threshold, and he will be your servant forever. You must do the same with your female servant.
Do not be troubled about sending him away from you free, because he has served you for six years for the wages of a hired farmworker. And the Lord your God will bless you in everything you do.
Consecrate to the Lord your God every firstborn male born among your cattle and sheep. Do not put your firstborn ox to work, and do not shear your firstborn sheep.
You and your household shall eat it before the Lord every year, in the place that the Lord your God chooses.
But if it has a defect—if it is blind or lame, or has any serious defect—do not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
Eat it in your town. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it together, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
But do not eat the blood. Pour it onto the ground like water.
Observe the month of Nisan and celebrate the Passover of the Lord your God, because in the month of Nisan you came out of the land of Egypt at night.
Slaughter sheep and cattle as the Passover sacrifice to the Lord your God, in the place that the Lord chooses for his name to be proclaimed there.

Do not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of suffering, because you came out of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
No leaven shall be seen anywhere within your territory for seven days, and none of the meat that you slaughter on the evening of the first day shall remain overnight until morning.
You may not slaughter the Passover sacrifice in any one of the towns that the Lord your God has given you.

Instead, in the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be proclaimed there, you shall slaughter the Passover sacrifice in the evening, when the sun sets, at the time when you came out of Egypt.
Boil it, roast it, and eat it in the place that the Lord your God chooses. In the morning, return and go into your homes.
Eat unleavened bread for six days. The seventh day is the closing assembly of the festival of the Lord your God. Do no work on it except what is done for sustenance.
Count seven weeks for yourself. Begin counting the seven weeks from when you begin reaping at harvest time.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks for the Lord your God, giving according to what your hand can afford and according to how much the Lord your God has blessed you.

Rejoice before your God—you, your sons and daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levite in your town, and the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow who are among you—in the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be proclaimed there.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and observe and carry out all these commands.
Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days, when you have gathered your produce from your threshing floor and your winepress.
Rejoice at your festival, together with your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow who lives in your town.
For seven days celebrate the festival of the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God chooses, with produce from all your harvest and from all the work of your hands, and rejoice.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God has chosen: at the festival of the law of Hallelujah, at the festival of the Sabbath, and at the festival of Booths. Do not come before the Lord your God empty-handed.
Each of you shall bring according to what your hands can afford and according to the blessing that the Lord your God has given you.
Appoint judges and recorders of tribute for yourselves in all the towns that the Lord your God has given you, tribe by tribe. They shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
They shall not show partiality or accept bribes, because a bribe blinds the wise and twists righteous words.
Pursue what is right with justice, so that you may live and enter to inherit the land that the Lord your God gives you.
Do not plant for yourself a tree to be worshiped, of any kind of wood, beside the altar of the Lord your God.
And do not act according to what the Lord your God hates.
Do not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect or anything wrong with it, for it is detestable to the Lord your God.
If a man or woman is found in one of your towns that the Lord your God has given you, doing evil before the Lord your God and violating his law,
and they have gone and worshiped other gods and bowed down to them—to the sun, the moon, or any of the heavenly host—which he did not command you,
then, when you hear about it, investigate thoroughly. If the report is true and this detestable thing has happened in Israel,
bring out that man, or that woman, and they shall stone them to death.
Those who are to be put to death shall be put to death on the testimony of two or three witnesses. They shall not be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
The hands of those witnesses shall be the first to put them to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Thus you shall remove evil from among you.

And if a matter of judgment is too difficult for you, between blood and blood, between cleanness and purification, or between injury and injury—matters of judgment within your towns—you shall rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be named there.
Go to the Levitical priests and to the judges who are serving in those days, and inquire. They shall make the judgment known to you.
Act according to the word they tell you at that place which the Lord has chosen for his name to be named there. Be careful to carry out all the law they teach you.
Act according to the judgment they tell you, and do not turn aside from the word they tell you, either to the right or to the left.

The man who acts arrogantly by refusing to obey the priest who stands and serves in the name of the Lord your God, or the judge who is serving in those days—that man shall die. Remove evil from Israel.
All the people shall hear and be afraid, and shall not sin again.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you as your inheritance, take possession of it, and live in it, and say, “I will appoint a king over myself, like all the nations around me,”
you shall appoint over yourself a king whom the Lord your God chooses from among your brothers. You may not appoint a foreign man over yourself, because he is not your brother.
He must not acquire many horses for himself, and he must not send the people back to Egypt, for the Lord has said, “You shall never return by that road again.”
He must not take many wives for himself, and his heart must not turn away. He must not accumulate great quantities of gold and silver for himself.
When he takes his seat as ruler, he shall write for himself in a book this copy of the law, from the one held by the priests and Levites.
And it shall remain with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn the way of the Lord his God, keep all his commandments, and carry out his judgments;

This is so that his heart will not become proud over his brothers, and so that he will not abandon the commandment of the Lord his God or turn aside to the right or to the left, so that he and his children may continue long in their rule among the Israelites.
The priests and Levites, and the whole tribe of Levi, shall have no inheritance with Israel. The offerings to the Lord are their portion, and they shall eat them.
They shall have no portion among their brothers, for the Lord is their portion, as he told them.
This is what is due to the priests from the people who slaughter a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the jaw, and the stomach.
You shall give him the first of your grain, the first of your wine, the first of your oil, and some of what you shear from your sheep.
For the Lord our God has chosen him from among all your tribes to stand before the Lord your God, to serve and to bless in his name, he and his children for all time.
If a Levite comes from one of your towns anywhere among the Israelites, where he has been living, because he desires with all his heart to serve at the place that the Lord your God has chosen,
And he shall serve in the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the Lord.
He shall receive his share and eat, apart from what comes from his sale in his hometown.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you, do not learn to practice the abominations of those nations.
Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in fire, practices divination, reads omens, or practices augury;
or who practices sorcery, casts spells, acts as a medium, summons the dead, or reads omens from birds.
For everyone who does these things is abhorrent to the Lord. Because of these abominations of theirs, the Lord will destroy them before you.
Be blameless before the Lord your God.
For those nations that you are dispossessing practice divination and listen to oracles, but it is not to be so with you.
The Lord your God has given you a prophet like me from among your brothers, and the Lord your God will raise him up for you. Listen to him in everything.

And everything that you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb on the day when you assembled, saying, “Let us no longer hear the voice of the Lord our God, nor see this great fire again, so that we do not die.”
The Lord said to me, “Everything they have said is true.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put my word in his mouth, and he will tell them what I command him.
As for the person who does not listen to that prophet in everything he says in my name, I myself will exact punishment from him.
But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet shall die.
If you say in your heart, ‘How can I recognize a word that the Lord has not spoken?’

Whatever a prophet speaks in the Lord’s name, if his word does not come to pass and things do not happen as he said, the Lord has not spoken that word. That prophet has spoken falsely, and you shall not listen to him.”
When the Lord your God destroys the nations whose land the Lord gives you, and you dispossess them and live in their land, in their towns, and in their houses,
set apart three towns for yourself in the midst of your land, which the Lord your God has given you.

Familiarize yourself with the roads to them, and divide into three parts the territory of your land, which the Lord your God has allotted to you, so that every person who kills someone may have a refuge there.
This is the law for the person who kills someone and flees there so that he may live: he must have killed the other person unintentionally and must not previously have been his enemy.

If someone goes with another person into the forest to cut wood, and strikes with the axe in his hand while cutting wood, and the iron head comes out of its wooden handle and falls on the other person and kills him, he shall flee to one of these towns and live;

so that the avenger of blood does not pursue the killer and follow him in the anger of his heart, overtake him because the road is long, and kill him, although he has committed no offense deserving death, since he was not previously the other person’s enemy.
For this reason I commanded you to do this, saying to you, “Set apart three towns for yourself.”
If the Lord enlarges your territory, as the Lord swore to your ancestors, and the Lord gives you all the land that the Lord said he would give to your ancestors,

provided that you obey and carry out this entire commandment that I give you today—to love the Lord your God and to walk in all his ways at all times—then you shall add three more towns for yourself to those three.
Thus innocent blood shall not be shed in your land, which the Lord your God has given you as your inheritance, and there shall be no bloodguilt among you.
But if a man hates another person, lies in wait for him, then rises against him and strikes him dead, and flees to one of these towns;
The elders of his town shall send for him, bring him back from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood, who shall kill him.
You shall show him no pity. You shall remove the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, and it will go well with you.
You shall not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, which your ancestors set up in your inheritance, in the land that the Lord your God gave you as your allotted possession.

One witness alone shall not give testimony against a person concerning any wrongdoing or any sin they have committed. Every matter shall be settled by the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses.
If they bring a malicious witness against a person, and he speaks falsely against him,
the two men who are disputing shall stand before the Lord, before the priests, and before the judges who hold office in those days.
The judges shall investigate and question them (and those two witnesses). As for the one who acted maliciously, gave false testimony, and stood against the other,
they shall do to him the harm he intended to do to the other. Thus you shall remove the evil from among you.
And others shall hear and be afraid, and shall not again do this evil thing among you.
And you shall show him no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot.

If you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
When you begin to fight, the priest shall come forward, speak to the people, and say to them:
“Listen, Israel! Today you are going out to fight your enemies. Do not lose heart, do not be afraid, do not be dismayed, and do not panic before them.
For the Lord your God goes with you all the way, to kill your enemies for you and to save you.”

And the officers shall say to the people, “If there is a man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it, let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man dedicate his house.”
If there is a man who has planted a vineyard but has not enjoyed its produce, let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man enjoy it.
If there is a man who has become engaged to a woman but has not married her, let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man marry her.

The scribes shall continue speaking to the people: “If there is a fearful man whose heart is afraid, let him go and return to his house, so that he does not make his fellow’s heart afraid like his own.”
When the scribes have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint officers of the army from among the leaders of the people.
When you approach a town to fight against it, you shall offer its people peace.
If they answer you peacefully and open the town to you, all the people found in it shall pay tribute to you and be subject to you.
But if they do not answer you and make war against you, you shall lay siege to it.
The Lord your God shall deliver it into your hands, and you shall kill all its males with the sword.

But the women, the goods, all the livestock, everything in the town, and all their possessions you shall take as plunder for yourself. Enjoy all the plunder of your enemies that the Lord your God has given you.
You shall do this to all the towns that are very far from you, which are not among the towns of these nations whose land the Lord your God gives you to possess.
You shall not leave alive anything that breathes.
Instead, you shall place the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites under the ban of complete destruction, as the Lord your God commanded you,
so that they do not teach you to practice all their abominations and everything they do for their gods, and you sin before the Lord your God.

If you besiege a city for many days, fighting against it to capture it, do not cut down its trees or bring iron against them. Instead, eat from them. Is a tree of the field a human being, that it should come before you and enter your siegeworks?
