But a tree that you know does not bear fruit you may cut down and fell, and build siegeworks against the city that is fighting with you, until you capture it.
If someone who has been killed is found lying in the open country in the land that the Lord your God has given you to possess, and his killer is unknown,
your leaders and officials shall go out and measure the distances to the cities surrounding the slain person.
The elders of the city nearest to the slain person shall bring a heifer from the herd that has not been put to work and has not pulled under a yoke.
And the elders of that city shall bring the heifer to a rugged valley that has not been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they shall cut the heifer’s tendons.
The priests and Levites shall come, for the Lord has chosen them to stand before him and bless in his name. By their word every dispute and every matter of pardon [?] shall be settled.
All the elders of the city nearest to the slain person shall wash their hands over the head of the heifer whose hamstrings they cut in the valley.
They shall speak and say, “Our hands did not shed this person's blood, nor did our eyes see it.”
Forgive your people Israel, Lord, whom you redeemed from the land of Egypt, so that guilt for taking a life may not rest upon your people Israel. And they will be forgiven for that life.
You shall remove the guilt of taking a life from among you, and it will go well with you if you do what is good and right before the Lord your God.
If you go out to war against your enemies, and the Lord your God delivers them into your hands, and you take captives from them,
and you see among the captives a woman of beautiful appearance, desire her, and take her for yourself to be your wife,
you shall bring her into your house, shave her head, and trim her nails.

You shall remove the clothes in which she was captured and have her stay in your house. She shall mourn her father and mother for thirty days. After this you may go in to her and live with her, and she shall become your wife.
Afterward, if you do not want her, you shall let her go free. You must not sell her for gold or deal treacherously with her, since you married her.
If a man marries two wives, hates one and loves the other, and the one he hates bears him his firstborn son,
when he leaves his possessions to his children, he may not give preference to the son of the wife he loves and disregard the son of the wife he hates.
He shall give him a double portion of everything he possesses, because he is the first of his children, and the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If a man has a rebellious and insolent son who does not obey his father or his mother, and they discipline him but he does not listen to them;
They shall take him to the leaders of his city and to the gate of his town.
They shall say to the people of their city, “This son of ours defies us and is arrogant. He does not listen to us, and he is a glutton and a drunkard.”
The people of his city shall stone him to death. You shall remove the evil from among you, and all Israel shall hear and be afraid.
If someone has sinned and his offense warrants a sentence of death, you shall hang him on a tree and kill him.

His body must not remain on the tree overnight. You must bury him that same day, because anyone hung on a tree is cursed before the Lord. Do not defile the land that the Lord your God gives you as your inheritance.
If you see your neighbor's ox or sheep straying on the road, do not ignore it. Bring it back to your neighbor and hand it over to him.

If your neighbor is not near you, or if you do not know him, gather the animal in and bring it into your house. It shall stay with you until your neighbor comes looking for it, and you shall return it to him.

You shall do the same with his donkey or his ox, and likewise with his clothing. You shall do this for anything your neighbor has lost, anything that has gone missing from him and that you have found. You may not ignore it.
If you see your neighbor’s donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not ignore them. Help him lift it up.
A woman must not dress in a man's attire, and a man must not wear a woman's clothing, for everyone who does this is detestable before the Lord your God.
If you come upon a bird’s brood before you on the road, in any tree or on the ground, whether chicks or eggs, do not take the mother with her young.
You must let the mother go free, but you may take her young for yourself, so that things may go well for you and your days may be many.
If you build a new house, you must make a parapet for your roof. Do not bring bloodshed into your house through someone falling from it.
You must not plant your vineyard with all kinds of different seeds, lest its produce be consecrated, both the seed you sow and the fruit of your vineyard.
You must not plow with a donkey and an ox together.
You must not wear clothing woven from wool and linen.
You must make twisted tassels for yourself on the four corners of the clothing you wear.
If a man hates the woman he has married after living with her,
and brings accusations against her and gives her a bad name, saying, “I married this woman, but when I slept with her, I did not find evidence of her virginity,”
her father and mother must take the cloth showing their daughter's virginity and bring it to the elders at the gate.
The girl's father shall say to the elders, “I gave this daughter of mine to this man to be his wife.

Now that he hates her, he has brought accusations against her, saying, ‘I did not find evidence of your daughter's virginity.’ But look, here is the cloth showing my daughter's virginity.” They shall spread out that cloth before the elders of that town.
The elders of that town shall seize that man and punish him.

They shall take a hundred shekels from him and give them to the girl's father, because he has given a virgin of Israel a bad name. She shall remain his wife, and he may not divorce her as long as he lives.
But if this accusation proves true, and no evidence of the girl's virginity is found,

they shall bring the girl out to the door of her father's house, and the men of that town shall stone her to death, because she has committed a disgraceful act among the children of Israel and committed sexual immorality in her father's house [?]. You shall remove evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, put both of them to death—the man who slept with the woman and the woman herself. You shall remove evil from Israel.
If a virgin girl is engaged to a man, and another man finds her in the town and sleeps with her,

bring both of them out to the gate of that town, and they shall stone them to death: the girl because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because he violated another man's wife. Remove evil from among you.
But if a man finds an engaged girl in the countryside, overpowers her, and sleeps with her, put only the man who slept with her to death.
Do nothing to the girl, because the girl has committed no offense deserving death. This case is like that of a man who attacks another man and kills him.
For he found her in the countryside, and the engaged girl cried out, but there was no one to help her.
If a man finds a virgin girl who is not engaged, overpowers her, and sleeps with her, and they are discovered,
the man who slept with the girl shall give her father fifty silver didrachmas. She shall become his wife, and he may not divorce her as long as he lives, because he violated her.
A man must not marry his father's wife or uncover his father's nakedness.
No one who has a bodily defect or has been castrated shall enter the house of the Lord.
So that they do not [?] the house of the Lord.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the house of the Lord, even to the third and fourth generation. Even to the tenth generation, and forever, they may not enter the house of the Lord.
For they did not welcome you with food and water on the road when you came out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But the Lord was unwilling to listen to Balaam, and the Lord turned his curse into a blessing, because the Lord your God loved you.
Do not speak of peace or well-being for them throughout all your days, forever.
Do not despise an Edomite, because he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you were a foreigner in their land.
The children born to them may enter the house of the Lord in the third generation.
When you go out to fight your enemies, guard yourself against every evil thing.
If there is a man among you who is unclean because of a nighttime emission, he must go outside the camp and must not enter the camp.
Toward evening he must wash his body with water, and when the sun has set, he may enter the camp.
Set aside a place for yourself outside the camp, where you can go outside.
Take a wooden implement with you in your belt. When you sit down, dig a hole, then get up and cover your excrement.

For the Lord your God walks about in your camp to save you and to deliver your enemies into your hands before you. Your camp must be holy, so that nothing shameful appears among you and he turns away from you and leaves you.
Do not return a slave to his master after he has been sold to you.
He is to live with you wherever he pleases, and you must not mistreat him.

There must be no prostitute among you from the daughters of Israel, and no male prostitute from the sons of Israel. There must be no one who brings [?] from among the daughters of Israel, and no one who brings [?] from among the sons of Israel.
Do not bring the earnings of prostitution or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God for any vow, for both are unclean before the Lord your God.
Do not charge your fellow Israelite interest: interest on gold, interest on food, or interest on anything you have lent him.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but you must not charge your fellow Israelite interest, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work in the land you are entering to possess.
If you make a vow to the Lord, do not delay fulfilling it, because the Lord your God will certainly demand it from you, and you will be guilty of sin.
But if you do not choose to make a vow, you are not guilty of sin.
But keep and carry out what has passed your lips. Give to the Lord as you vowed; do exactly what you said with your mouth.
If you enter another person's field, you may pluck ears of grain with your hands, but you must not bring a sickle into another person's field.
If you enter another person's vineyard, eat grapes until you are satisfied, but do not put any into a container.

If a man takes a wife and lives with her, and afterward she finds no favor with him because he has found something shameful in her, he is to write her a certificate of divorce, put it into her hands, and send her out of his house.
She then goes away and marries another man.
If that later husband also hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it into her hands, and sends her out of his house, or if that later husband who took her as his wife dies,

the first husband, who sent her away, may not return to her and take her as his wife after she has become defiled. For this thing is unclean before the Lord your God. Do not defile the land that the Lord your God is giving you as your inheritance.
If a man has taken a wife, he must not go out to war, nor must any duty be imposed on him. He must be free at home for one year, so that he may rejoice with the wife he has married.
Do not take a mill or its upper millstone as a pledge, for it is a means of sustaining life, and it must not be taken as a pledge.
If a man is found to have kidnapped someone from among his fellow Israelites, enslaved him, and sold him, that kidnapper must be put to death. You must remove evil from among you.
Watch yourself concerning signs of leprosy. Be very careful to carry out every instruction that the priests and Levites give you. Be careful to act as I have commanded you.
Remember everything that the Lord your God did to Miriam on the road when you came out of Egypt.
If your neighbor owes you a debt of any kind, do not enter his house to take your pledge.
You must stand outside, and the debtor who owes you must himself bring the pledge outside to you.
If he is a poor man, do not keep his pledge with you overnight.
Return his pledge to him at sunset, so that he may sleep in his garment and you may be blessed. This will count as a righteous deed for you before the Lord your God.
Do not withhold the wages of your poor and needy hired worker, whether he is one of your own people or one of the foreigners living in your town.
Give him his wages in the morning, and do not let the sun set on them, because he is poor and depends on them. Then he will not cry out against you to the Lord, and you will not incur sin.
Parents must not be put to death because of their children, nor must children be put to death because of their parents. Each person must be put to death for his own wrongdoing.
Do not pervert justice for a foreigner, an orphan, or a widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you harvest the grain of your field and forget a sheaf in your field, do not go back to take it. It must be for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

When you harvest your vineyard, do not go back over it to gather every remaining grape. What remains must be for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
When you harvest your olives, do not go back over them to gather everything that remains. What remains must be for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you were a foreigner in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
If there is a dispute between people and they come to court to have their case judged, the judges shall acquit the one who is right and condemn the one who is wrong;
If the condemned man is to be flogged, they must make him sit before the court and flog him in their presence, in proportion to his offense.
They must give him forty lashes by count, and no more. If they increase his flogging beyond this, you will have humiliated your brother before you.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

If brothers live together, one with the other, and one of them dies without children, his wife must not marry an unrelated man who is not his kinsman. Her husband's brother must marry her and go in to her. She must become his wife, and he must live with her.
The child who is born must belong to the man who died and be called by his name, so that his name may not be erased from Israel.
If the man does not want to marry his brother's wife, the woman must go up to the elders at the gate and say, "My husband's brother does not want to preserve his brother's name in Israel."
The elders of his town must summon him and say to him, "Do you not want to raise up offspring for your brother in Israel?" He will stand and say, "I do not want to marry her."

Then that woman shall come before (the Lord and before) the elders of that town, untie the sandal from one of his feet, spit in his face, and say, “This is what shall be done to the man who does not build up his brother’s household.”
And his name in Israel shall be “The household of the man whose sandal was untied.”

If two men are fighting together, one man with another, and the wife of one of them comes to rescue her husband from the hands of the man striking him, and reaches out her hand and seizes him by his two testicles,
they shall cut off her hands, and your eye shall show no pity.
Do not keep for yourself a small measure and a large measure.
You shall not keep in your house a large measure and a small measure.
Your balance shall be accurate and fair, so that your days may be many [in the land] that the Lord your God gives you as your inheritance.
For everyone who does this, and everyone who acts unjustly, is detestable to the Lord your God.
Remember everything Amalek did to you on the road when you came out of the land of Egypt:
how he confronted you on the road and cut off those in your traveling company who were struggling behind you, while you were hungry and exhausted, and you did not fear God.

When the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you, in the land that the Lord your God gives you to possess as your inheritance, you shall wipe out Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you to possess as your inheritance, and settle in it,
you shall take some of the produce of the land that the Lord your God has given you, put it in a basket, and go to the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be proclaimed there.
You shall go to the priest who is serving in those days and say to him, “Today I declare to the Lord my God that I have arrived in the land that the Lord swore to our ancestors to give us.”
The priest shall take that basket from your hands and place it on the altar of the Lord your God.
You shall say before the Lord your God, “My father left Syria and went down to Egypt. He lived there when they were few in number, and there he became a great nation, very populous and numerous.”
“The Egyptians tormented us, afflicted us, and made us perform harsh labor.
We cried out to the Lord, the God of our ancestors, and the Lord heard our voice. He saw our suffering, and the Lord saw our toil and our torment.
The Lord himself brought us out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, with great terror, with a great sign, and with wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now I have brought the first produce of my land, which the Lord has given me, a land flowing with milk and honey.” Then you shall bow down before the Lord your God.
You shall rejoice in every blessing that the Lord your God has given you—you and your household, together with the Levite and the foreign resident who lives among you.

When you have finished setting aside all the tithes of the produce of your land in the third year, then, when you tithe a second time, you shall give it to the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow. They shall eat it in your town and be satisfied.

You shall say before the Lord your God, “I have cleared from my house what is consecrated to you and have given it to the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow, according to every commandment you commanded me. I have not transgressed your commandment or forgotten it.

I have not eaten any of it in my suffering, nor sacrificed any of it to what is unclean, nor placed any of it on a corpse. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God; I have obeyed what he commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land that you have given them, which you swore to our ancestors to give us—a land flowing with milk and honey.”
Today the Lord your God has commanded you to carry out all these statutes, to keep his law, and to carry it out with all your heart and all your soul.
You shall worship the Lord your God, walk in his ways, keep his law and his statutes, and obey his voice.
For the Lord has chosen you today to be his own people, as he said, so that you may keep all his commandments;
You shall be above all nations, and he will give you a great name, praise, and honor, so that you may be a holy people to the Lord your God, as he has said.
Moses commanded the elders of Israel and said to them, “Be careful to carry out all these commandments, everything that I command you today.
When you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God is giving you, you shall set up large stones for yourself and coat them with white plaster.

You shall write all the words of this law on those stones after you cross the Jordan, when you enter the land that the Lord, the God of our fathers, is giving you (so that he may give you)—a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, told you.
When you cross the Jordan, you shall set up those stones about which I command you today on Mount Ebal, and coat them with white plaster.
There you shall build an altar to the Lord your God out of stones, and no iron shall touch them.
You shall build an altar to the Lord your God with stones that have not been hewn.
You shall offer sacrifices of well-being upon them. Eat and be satisfied there, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
Write all this law on those stones very clearly.
Moses and the priests said to the Levites and to all Israel, “Be silent and listen, Israel. On this day you have become the people of the Lord your God.”
Obey the voice of the Lord your God and carry out all his commandments and his statutes that I command you today.”
Moses commanded the people that day and said to them:
“These are the ones who shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people after you cross the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
These are the ones who shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
The Levites shall respond [?] and say to all Israel in a loud voice:
‘Cursed be the man who makes a carved or cast image, something detestable to the Lord, the work of a craftsman, and sets it up and hides it.’ And all the people shall answer and say, ‘Amen and amen.’
Cursed be anyone who dishonors his father and his mother. And all the people shall say, “Amen and amen.”
‘Cursed be anyone who steals his neighbor’s boundary marker.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who denies justice to a foreign resident, an orphan, or a widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife, because he has exposed his father’s nakedness.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with any animal.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with his sister, whether she is his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with his wife’s mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who strikes another person in secret.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
‘Cursed be every person who does not uphold and carry out the words of this law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen and amen.’
If you diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God and take care to carry out all his commandments that I command you today, the Lord your God will set you above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come upon you and reach you if you obey the voice of the Lord your God.
You will be blessed in the field, and you will be blessed in the city.
The fruit of your womb will be blessed, as will the crops of your land, your herds of cattle, and your flocks of sheep.
Your storehouses and your surplus will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you come in, and you will be blessed when you go out.
The Lord your God will cause your enemies who rise against you to be crushed beneath your feet. They will come out against you by one road and flee from you by seven roads.
The Lord will send his blessing upon your houses and upon everything you put your hand to, in the land that the Lord your God has given you.
The Lord will establish you as a holy people for himself, just as the Lord swore to your ancestors, if you obey the voice of the Lord your God and walk in his ways.
All the nations of the earth will see that the Lord's name has been placed upon you, and they will fear you.

The Lord your God will make you abound in good things through the children of your womb and the crops of your land, and he will make your livestock reproduce in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give you, for as long as the heavens are above the earth.

The Lord will open for you his blessed storehouse, the heavens, to give your land rain in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.

The Lord will make you the head and not the tail. You will be above and not below, if you obey the voice of the Lord your God and all his commandments that I command you today, taking care to carry them out.
Do not turn aside from any of the words that I command you today, either to the right or to the left, to follow other gods and worship them.
But if you do not obey the voice of the Lord your God and keep all his commandments that I command you today, all these curses will come upon you and reach you.
You will be cursed in the field and in the city.
Your storehouses and your surplus will be cursed.
The children of your womb will be cursed, as will the crops of your land, your herds of cattle, and your flocks of sheep.
You will be cursed when you come in, and you will be cursed when you go out.

The Lord will send upon you destitution, famine, and turmoil. Everything you put your hand to will perish, and he will uproot you until he quickly wipes you out because of your evil deeds, because he has abandoned me.
The Lord will bring death upon you until he destroys you from the land you are entering to possess.
The Lord will strike you with wasting disease, fever, jaundice, fear, terror, drought, and crop failure. They will pursue you until they destroy you.
The heavens above your head will become bronze for you, and the earth beneath you will become iron.
The Lord will turn the rain of your land into dust, and dirt will fall upon you from heaven until it crushes you and destroys you.
The Lord will cause you to be slain before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road and flee from them by seven roads. You will be scattered throughout all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your corpses will become food for the birds of the sky, and you will find no one to bury you.
The Lord will strike you with the plague of Egypt, with a painful eruption on your private parts, and with itching for which there is no cure.
The Lord will strike you with madness, blindness, and terror of heart.
You will grope about in the daytime as a blind person gropes in darkness, and you will not find the way. You will be oppressed and robbed all your days, and you will find no one to help you.
You will marry a woman, but another man will take her away from you. You will build a house but will not live in it. You will plant a vine but will not gather its fruit.

They will slaughter your ox, but you will not eat any of it. They will take your donkey away from you and will not return it to you. Your sheep will pass to servants and to your enemy, and you will find no one to help you.
Your sons and daughters will pass to another people. You will see with your own eyes how they oppress them, and there will be nothing you can do.
A people you do not know will eat the produce of your land and the fruit of your labor. You will be oppressed and tormented all your days.
You will become [?] because of what your eyes see, and you will not see.
The Lord will strike you with a painful disease in your knees, your thighs, and your legs, from which you cannot recover, from the soles of your feet to your head.
The Lord will take you and the rulers you appointed for yourselves into a great nation that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will worship other gods, wood and stone.
There you will be terrified, and you will become a byword and a subject of talk among all the nations among whom, and to whom, the Lord takes you.
You will take much seed out into your fields but bring little in, because locusts will eat it.
You will plant a vineyard and cultivate it, but you will not drink its wine or enjoy it, because worms will eat it.
You will possess olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with their oil, because their fruit will fall off.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not be left to you, for they will be taken away and led into captivity.
[?] will destroy all the produce of your land and all the growth of your trees.
The foreigner who lives among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you will be below.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be your head, and you will be his tail.

All these curses will come upon you, pursue you, and overtake you until they destroy you and wipe you out, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God and keep his commandments and all his ordinances that he commanded you.
It will be a sign and a wonder upon you and upon your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a glad heart when you had an abundance of everything.
You will serve the enemies whom the Lord sends against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he destroys you.
The Lord will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, like an eagle swooping down—a nation whose speech you do not understand;
A nation with a fierce face, which does not respect the elderly or show mercy to the young;
He will destroy the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your land until he leaves you no grain, wine, or oil, no herds of cattle or flocks of sheep, until he destroys you.

He will wipe you out in all your towns until he brings down your great towers and the fortifications you trust in throughout your territory. He will torment you in all your towns that the Lord your God gave you.
You will eat the offspring of your womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom he gave you, in the distress and torment with which your enemy torments you in your towns.
Even the tender and delicate man among you will look with horror at his brother, at the wife in his embrace, and at the remaining children whom they have left to them.
They will give each of them the flesh of their children to eat, because they will leave them nothing, in the torment and distress with which your enemies torment you in all your towns.
The woman among you who is delicate and weak, who [?] her feet to walk on the ground because she is delicate and weak, will look begrudgingly at the husband in her embrace, her son, and her daughter.

And she will secretly eat her own flesh that comes from between her limbs, and the children she has borne, when she lacks everything, in the distress and suffering with which your enemy afflicts you within your towns.
If you do not obey and carry out all the words of this law written in this book, so that you fear this honored and glorious name, that of the Lord your God.
And the Lord will make your plagues and the plagues of your descendants extraordinary: great and astonishing plagues, and terrible disease and suffering.
He will bring back upon them all those evil diseases of Egypt which you did not fear (from which you did not fear) when confronted with them, and they will cling to you.
The Lord will bring upon you every disease and every plague that is not written in this book of the law, until he destroys you and you are wiped out.
And you will be left few in number, though you were as numerous as the stars of heaven, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
And just as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and make you numerous, so the Lord will rejoice over you to uproot you, and you will perish from the land that you are entering to possess.
And the Lord will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods, stone and wood, which neither you nor your ancestors have known.
And there among those nations he will give you no rest and will not allow your foot a place to stand. There the Lord will give you a sorrowful heart, failing eyes, and a wasting soul.
And your life will hang suspended before your eyes, and you yourself will be terrified by day [and by night], and you will have no confidence in your life.

When morning comes, you will say, “If only evening would come!” And when evening comes, you will say, “If only morning would come!” This will be because of the fear in your heart that terrifies you, and because of what is shown before your eyes and what you see.

And the Lord will bring you back to Egypt on donkeys, and by land on foot, to that land of which he said, “You shall never see it again.” There you will become male and female slaves to your enemies, and no one will show you mercy.
And these are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that he made with them at Horeb.
And Moses summoned all the Israelites and said to them, “You yourselves have seen everything that the Lord did for you in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, to his officials, and to all his land;
the great plagues that your eyes saw, and those great signs and wonders, and the strong hand and uplifted arm.
And the Lord has not given you a heart to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day.
And he led you for forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes did not wear out, nor did your sandals wear out on your feet;
while you ate no bread and drank no wine or mead, for you arrived at this place so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.
And Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Moab came out to meet you and fight against you, and we killed them.
And we took their land, and I gave that land to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
And take care to carry out all the words of this covenant, so that you may understand everything you do.
And now all of you stand before the Lord your God: the great men of your tribes, your leaders, your officials, your scribes, and all the men of Israel;
and your wives, your children, and the foreign resident who is among your tents, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water;
so that you may hear the covenant of the Lord your God and the curse of the Lord your God, which he has established with you today.
So that he may make you his people and may himself be your God, as he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And it is not with you alone that I establish this covenant and this curse;
but also with those who are here with you today before the Lord your God, and with those who are not here with you today.
For you yourselves know how we lived in Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of those nations and went beyond them.
And you saw their unclean things and their gods of wood, stone, silver, and gold, which they made for themselves.

Let there be no man or woman, people or tribe, or anyone among you whose heart turns away from the Lord your God and who goes to worship these gods of the nations. Let there be no evil root among you that sprouts and bears poison and bitterness.

And when you hear the words of this curse, whoever says in his heart, “I will be forgiven, because I acted and walked according to the folly of my heart,” so that death [?] will not sweep away the sinner along with the innocent.

The Lord will not be willing to forgive him. Instead, at that time the Lord’s anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse of this covenant written in this book of the law will pursue him. The Lord will erase his name from under heaven.
And the Lord will bring him into disaster and separate him from all the children of Israel, according to every curse of this covenant written in this book of the law.

The later generation, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land will speak when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases that the Lord has sent upon it;

Sulfur and salt will burn throughout that whole land. It will not be sown or produce growth, and no green plant will come up in it, just as Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim were overthrown, which the Lord overthrew in his anger.
And all the nations will say, “Why has the Lord done this to this land? And what is the fury of this great anger?”
And they will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, which he made with their ancestors when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
They went and worshiped other gods and bowed down to them, gods they did not know and that could not benefit them.
And the Lord’s anger burned against this land, and he brought upon it every curse written in this book of the law.
And the Lord uprooted them from their land in anger, fury, and great punishment, as it is now.”
What is hidden belongs to the Lord our God, but what is revealed belongs to us and our children forever, so that we may do everything this law says.
And when all these things come upon you, both the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, remember them in your heart among all the nations where the Lord has scattered you.
And return to the Lord your God and obey his voice in everything I command you today, with all your heart and all your soul.
And the Lord will forgive all your sins and have mercy on you, and the Lord will gather you again from all the nations among which he has scattered you.
Even if he has scattered you to the ends of heaven, the Lord your God will gather you from there.
And the Lord your God will bring you into the land that your ancestors possessed, so that you may possess it. He will do good to you, multiply you, and make you more numerous than your ancestors.
And the Lord will soften your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, and so that you and your descendants may live.
And the Lord your God will bring this curse upon your enemies, upon those who hate you, and upon those who persecuted you.
But you, return and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and carry out all his commandments that I command you today.

And the Lord your God will make you prosper greatly in all the work of your hands, in your children, in the crops of your land, and in the offspring of your livestock. For the Lord your God will again rejoice over you in doing good to you, just as he rejoiced over your ancestors.

Because you have obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and carrying out all his commandments, all his judgments, and his laws written in this book of the law, if you return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
For this commandment that I command you today is not too difficult, nor is it far from you.
It is not in heaven, so that you would say, “Who will go up to heaven for us and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and carry it out?”
Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you would say, “Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us and make us hear it, so that we may carry it out?”
For look, the word is very near you, in your mouth, in your heart, and in your hands, so that you may carry it out.
And look, today I have set before you life and death, good and evil.

If you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and to all his commandments that I command you today—to love the Lord your God, walk in all his ways, and keep his statutes and judgments—you will multiply and live, and the Lord your God will bless you throughout the land you are entering to possess.
But if your heart turns away, and you refuse to listen, and you go astray and bow down to other gods,
I declare to you today that you will certainly perish. Your days will not be long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.
I call heaven and earth to witness before you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Choose life for yourself, so that you and your descendants may live.

Love the Lord your God, listen to his voice, and hold firmly to him, for he is your life. Through him your days will be prolonged, so that you may live in the land that the Lord swore to give your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses finished speaking these words to all the Israelites.
He said to them, “I am a hundred and twenty years old today, and I can no longer go in and out. Moreover, the Lord has told me, ‘You shall not cross this Jordan.’
The Lord himself goes before you; he will destroy these nations before you.
As the Lord has said, so the Lord will deal with them, just as he dealt with Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan, and with their land,
just as he destroyed them. The Lord handed them over to you, and you dealt with them as I commanded you.
Be courageous and strong. Do not be afraid, alarmed, or dismayed before them, for the Lord your God himself goes before you and is with you. He will not leave you or abandon you.”

Moses called Joshua and said to him before all Israel, “Be courageous and strong, for you will go before this people into the land that the Lord swore to give your ancestors, and you will enable them to inherit it.
The Lord, who goes with you, will not leave you or abandon you. Do not be afraid or alarmed.”
Moses wrote the words of this law in a book and gave it to the priests, the descendants of Levi who carry the ark of the Lord’s law, and to the elders of the Israelites.
Moses commanded them that day, saying, “At the end of seven years, in the year of release, at the Feast of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord your God in the place he has chosen, read this law before Israel.

Gather the people to listen—the men, the women, the children, and the foreigners living in your towns—so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God, and, having heard, may carry out all the laws contained in these words.
Their children also, who do not know, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days they live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Your time to die is approaching. Call Joshua and stand at the entrance of the tent, and I will give him instructions.” Moses and Joshua went into the tent of testimony.
The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent of testimony.

The Lord said to Moses, “You are about to sleep with your ancestors. This people will rise up and prostitute themselves by following the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me and violate my covenant that I made with them.

My anger will blaze against them on that day. I will abandon them and turn my face away from them, and they will become food for their enemies. Many evils and sufferings will overtake them, and they will say on that day, “Because the Lord my God has abandoned me and is not with us, this disaster has overtaken us.”
And I will certainly turn my face away from them on that day because of all the sins they have committed, turning to foreign gods.
Now write down the words of this song and teach it to the children of Israel. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for me against the children of Israel.

For I will bring them into the blessed land that I swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey. When they have eaten and are satisfied, they will grow fat and turn to other gods and worship them. They will provoke me and abandon my covenant.

This song will stand before them as a witness against them, because it will not be forgotten from their mouths or from the mouths of their children. For I know all the evil they will do here, even before I bring them into that blessed land which I swore to their ancestors.
Moses wrote down this song on that day and taught it to the children of Israel.
Moses commanded Joshua and said to him, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the children of Israel into the land that the Lord swore to their fathers, and he will be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book,
he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the Lord’s law, saying to them:
“Take this book and place it inside the ark of the law of the Lord your God, and let it remain there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebelliousness and your stubborn neck. Even while I am still alive today, you have rebelled against the Lord. How much more will you do so after my death!

Gather before me the elders of your tribes, your leaders, your officials, and your scribes, so that I may speak to them and they may hear all these words. I will call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after my death you will commit grave sins and abandon the way I commanded you to follow. Disaster will come upon you in the latter days, because you will do evil before the Lord your God, provoking him to anger by the work of your hands.”
Moses spoke all the words of this song to the whole assembly of Israel, making them hear it in full. He said:
“Listen, heaven, and I will speak; hear, earth, the words of my mouth.
Receive my words like rain, and let my speech fall like dew, like rain upon the fields and like mist upon the grass.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord. Give glory to our God.
The Lord is righteous in his deeds, and all his ways are upright. The Lord is righteous, and there is no injustice in him. The Lord is righteous and good.
They have sinned, and these unclean children are not his—a rebellious and perverse generation.
Is this how you repay the Lord, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not the Father who created you? He created you and made you.
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you; ask the elders, and they will inform you.
When the Most High apportioned the nations, and when he scattered the children of Adam, he established the nations, each within its boundaries, according to the number of the angels of God.
Jacob became the Lord’s portion, his people, and Israel the allotted share of his inheritance.
He satisfied them in the wilderness, in a land of thirst and heat, in a desert land. He sustained them, led them, and guarded them like the pupil of an eye.
Like an eagle gathering its young beneath its wings and embracing its young against its sides, he bore them on his wings and carried them on his back.
The Lord alone led them, and no foreign god was with him.
He brought them up to the rich land and fed them the produce of the fields. He nursed them with honey from the rock and oil from hard stone,
with butter from young cattle and milk from sheep, with the fat of goats and cattle, young cattle and sheep, and with the finest wheat. They drank the blood of grapes as wine.
Jacob ate and was satisfied, and the beloved kicked from being full. He grew fat, thick, and broad. He abandoned God his creator and turned away from God his life.
They provoked me with what was foreign and embittered me with their uncleanness.
They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods they did not know, newly arrived gods who are of no use and whom their fathers did not know.
He abandoned God who gave you birth, and you forgot God who nursed you.
God saw and became jealous, and his anger burned against their sons and daughters.
He said, “I will turn my face away from them and see what becomes of them in the end, for they are a generation of rebels, children who have no faith.
They made me jealous with what is not God and angered me with their gods. I will make them jealous with what is not a people and anger them with a people who have no understanding.
For a fire burns from my anger and blazes down to the depths of Sheol. It devours the earth and its produce and burns the foundations of the mountains.
I will gather them for calamity and spend all my arrows against them.

They will perish from hunger and become food for birds, and their strength will fail. I will send against them the teeth of the wild beasts of the earth, together with venom, so that they flee from the land.
Outside, slaughter will rob them of their children; inside their houses there will be terror, for their young men together with their young women, and their infants together with their old men.
I said that I would scatter them and erase their memory from the earth and from humankind.
Because of the enemy's anger, [?], lest the enemy grow arrogant and say, ‘Our own hand was strong; it was not God who did all this.’
For they are a people devoid of counsel, and they have neither discernment nor faith.
They did not think to understand this or to understand it in the days to come.
How could one put a thousand to flight, and two drive away ten thousand? For God sold them, and our God handed them over.
For their gods are not like our God, and our enemies are fools.
For their vineyard is like the vineyard of Sodom, and their vines are from Gomorrah. Their grape clusters are clusters of gall, and their berries are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents of the earth, the deadly venom of vipers.
Is not this command from me, sealed in my storehouses?
On the day of judgment I will take vengeance on them, and in due time their feet will slip. For the day of their destruction has drawn near; it has arrived and is ready for you.”
For the Lord will judge his people and plead the cause of his servants, because he sees that they have wasted away and perished and have been abandoned where they are.
And when they [?], God said, “Where are your gods in whom you trust?
You who eat the fat of their sacrifices and drink the wine of their drink offerings—let them rise and help you, and let them be your salvation.
Know, know that I am he, and there is no other God besides me. I kill and bring to life; I punish and show mercy. There is no one who can rescue from my hand.
For I will raise my hand to heaven and swear by my right hand and say, ‘I live forever.’
I will sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand will be ready for judgment. I will repay my adversaries with vengeance and take revenge on those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with their blood, and my sword will devour their flesh, from the blood of the slain and the captives, and the heads of the enemy’s messengers.

Let all the heavens rejoice together, and let all the angels of God bow down to him. Let the nations rejoice with their peoples, and let all the children of God say, “He is mighty!” For he will avenge the blood of his children. He will take vengeance and repay his adversaries with vengeance, and he will repay those who hate him. The Lord will cleanse the land for his people.
Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the children of Israel. Moses came and spoke to the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
And when Moses had finished speaking to all Israel;
He said to them, “Keep in your hearts all these words that I have declared to you today. Command your children today to observe and carry out all the words of this law.
For these words are not empty words for you; they are your life. Through these words your days will be prolonged in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
The Lord spoke to Moses on that day and said to him:
“Go up to Mount Abarim, which is on Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the children of Israel to possess.
Die on the mountain that you ascend there, and join your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.

For you disobeyed my word among the children of Israel at the gathering at the waters of contention, at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not uphold my holiness among the children of Israel.
Look at that land before you, but you will not enter it.”
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before he died.
He said, “The Lord came from Sinai and also appeared in Seir. He rested on Mount Paran with the myriads of Kadesh, those at his right, his angels, and those with him.”
He had mercy on his people and on those sanctified by his hands; these too are yours.
They received through his voice the law that Moses commanded us, an inheritance for the people of Jacob.
There will be a messenger among the beloved when the messengers of the nations gather with the tribe of Israel.
Keep Reuben alive, and let him not die; let his numbers be great.
And this concerning Judah: “Hear Judah’s voice, Lord, and let him return to his people. Let his hands judge for him, and be his helper against his enemies.”
Concerning Levi he said, “Return to Levi his word and his righteousness, to the righteous man whom they tested with a trial and with whom they contended at the waters of contention.
He said to his father and mother, ‘I have not seen you.’ He did not acknowledge his brothers or take notice of his children, but he kept your word and held firmly to your covenant,
so that they might teach your judgments to Jacob and your law to Israel, and offer incense against your anger, and continually at your altar.
Bless his strength, Lord, and accept the work of his hands. Bring down a heavy burden upon his enemies who oppose him; do not raise up those who hate him.”
Concerning Benjamin he said, “The Lord’s beloved will dwell securely. The Lord will shelter him all his days, and he will rest between his shoulders.”
Concerning Joseph he said, “His land has the blessing of the Lord, the rain of heaven and dew, and the spring of the deep beneath it,
its produce in each season, from the rising of the sun and from the succession of the months.
May it surpass the tops of the mountains and the tops of the everlasting hills.
The land is always abundant and pleasing to him who appeared in the bush. May this come upon Joseph’s head, and may his head be honored among his brothers.

His beauty is like that of a firstborn bull, and his horns are the horns of a one-horned beast. With them he will gore the nations together, to the ends of the earth. These are the tens of thousands of Ephraim, and these are the tens of thousands of Manasseh.”
Concerning Zebulun he said, “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your dwellings.”
But they will destroy the nations. Call there and offer righteous sacrifices, for the wealth of the sea will sustain you, and the possessions of those who live along the coast.
And to Gad he said, “May Gad's blessing be broad, like a lion crushing the arm of rulers.”

He saw his first portion, for there they divided the land of rulers, while the princes were gathered together with the ruler of the people and with the people of Israel. The Lord carried out his judgment and his righteousness with Israel.
And to Dan he said, “Dan is a lion's cub, and he will leap out from Bashan.”
And to Naphtali he said, “Naphtali is satisfied with good things and will be filled with the Lord's blessing. Let him inherit the sea and the southwest.”
And to Asher he said, “Asher is blessed among the children. May he be favored by his brothers, and may he wash his feet in oil.”
His sandals are iron and bronze. May your strength last as long as your days.
There is none like the God of the beloved. He who dwells in heaven is your helper, and the greatness of his splendor is in heaven.
The Lord will shelter you completely with the strength of everlasting arms. He will drive the enemy out from before you, as he said that he would destroy them.
You will settle Israel securely, alone in the land of Jacob, in a land of wheat and wine. Heaven, too, is yours, with clouds and dew.
Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people whom the Lord saves? Your helper strengthens you, and your glory is in your sword. Your enemies have lied, but you will tread on their necks.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah, opposite Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land of Gilead,
and all the land of Naphtali, all the land of Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
and the wilderness and the regions of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Seir.

The Lord said to Moses, “This is the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, telling them, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ Look, I have shown it to you with your own eyes, but you will not enter there.”
Moses, the Lord's servant, died in the land of Moab, according to the Lord's word.
They buried him in the ground near Beth Peor, and no one knows his burial place to this day.
Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died, and his eyes had neither grown dim nor deteriorated.
The children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, for thirty days. Then the days of mourning during which they wept for Moses came to an end.
Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. All the children of Israel obeyed him and did everything as the Lord had commanded Moses.
No prophet like Moses arose again in Israel, one who spoke with the Lord face to face,
in all the signs and wonders that the Lord sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, his officials, and his land,
the great wonders, the mighty hand, and the uplifted arm—all that Moses did before all Israel.
